textos: Why did Madrid blow up a market in 1974?
In 1934, the Republic built a market that filled the whole Plaza de Olavide.
An octagon inside an octagonal square, by Javier Ferrero, the city architect.
Stepped roofs around a large central courtyard that ventilated the whole market.
Not one ornament: reinforced-concrete pilasters and deep beams.
And underneath, vehicles drove straight through it.
Forty years later, the City Council decided to demolish it. Neighbours protested.
A controlled blast. In seconds, the market was gone.
In its place: gardens and a car park for 400 cars.
Today the square is the heart of the neighbourhood. Better a square than a market?
